title: Stress, strain, and elastic response
objective: Relate tensile, shear, and bulk stress to deformation within a stated linear elastic regime and propagate measurement limits.

officialScope.requirement: NU's PHS 231 description explicitly includes statics, elasticity, and fracture. This lesson supplies elasticity; m08-l03 supplies plasticity, fracture, and evidence limits.
officialScope.distinction: Lesson ordering, examples, synthetic material properties, supported apparatus models, 18 practice variants, four-question checkpoint, and rubric are proposed teaching choices. No official equipment requirement, independent subject review, or pilot validation has been established.

prerequisites.purpose: Internal-force cuts, support forces, static candidates, and compatibility for redundant supports.
Squared and cubed unit conversion, finite allowed bounds, and measurement resolution.
Quasistatic work as an integral and the factor one half for linear force growth.
Recoverable energy versus dissipated energy and model validity.
Integrals of varying axial force and derivatives of energy; develop the needed calculus locally.

coverage.teaching: Two opposite end forces can give zero external resultant while leaving nonzero internal axial force. Isolate one side of a cut; do not sum the magnitudes of the two end forces. Nominal normal stress uses original cross-sectional area; tensile sign positive, compression negative. Uniform stress is an approximation away from load introductions and flaws.
critical: Zero resultant does not imply zero deformation.
A pair of end forces of magnitude F gives nominal stress F/A, not 2F/A.

coverage.teaching: Pa=N/m²; MPa=N/mm²; GPa=1000MPa. Square the length conversion for area and cube it for volume. Engineering strain=(L-L0)/L0, not L/L0. State percentage and microstrain conventions. Circular area πd²/4, not πd². Original versus deformed area distinguished, with engineering quantities used throughout.
critical: Strain is dimensionless and is not a displacement.

coverage.teaching: Derive sigma=E epsilon, delta=F L0/(E A0), k=E A0/L0, compliance=1/k. Material modulus differs from specimen stiffness. Signed compression allowed only in a supplied short, laterally supported ideal model; no buckling criterion inferred. Compare fixed-force and fixed-displacement experiments.
critical: A modulus is not a spring constant.
A larger area changes stiffness but not the material's E.
Boundary conditions determine the effect of changing geometry.

coverage.teaching: Engineering shear gamma=delta_x/h≈angle for small angles in radians; tau=G gamma; tau is tangential force per loaded face area. A homogeneous static shear element needs complementary face tractions to balance moments. Hydrostatic pressure increment Δp positive in compression gives volumetric strain ΔV/V0=-Δp/K, compressibility1/K. Shear uses shape change, bulk uses volume change; fluids have no static shear modulus within the simple fluid model.
critical: Use the area of the sheared face and transverse height.
Do not drop the minus sign in bulk strain.
Do not multiply equal pressure forces on different faces into a net compressive force.

coverage.teaching: Integrate gradually increasing force from the stress-free reference. U=F delta/2=F²L/(2EA)=EA delta²/(2L), with energy density u=sigma²/(2E). Corresponding shear u=tau²/(2G) and bulk incremental u=(Δp)²/(2K). Explain zero closed-cycle work only inside a validated reversible linear range; full loading/unloading beyond that range is not determined by E.
critical: Final force times full displacement misses the one-half factor.
Energy remains nonnegative for signed compression.
Elastic and linear are distinct properties.

coverage.teaching: Series members share axial force and add extensions; parallel members between translation-only rigid plates share end displacement and add forces. Derive equivalent stiffness and check each member's range separately. Integrate N(x)/(E(x)A(x)) for a supplied variable axial-force model; include a hanging bar's own weight without assuming uniform stress.
critical: Parallel load sharing is proportional to stiffness only under the stated compatibility and preload assumptions.
An average stress does not locate the peak stress.
Buckling and bending are outside the simple axial model.

coverage.teaching: Introduce Poisson ratio ν=-epsilon_transverse/epsilon_axial in uniaxial loading. With homogeneous isotropic small-strain elasticity only, give E=2G(1+ν)=3K(1-2ν); positive finite E,G,K imply -1<ν<1/2. Derive small volume strain as the sum of three normal strains. Label this a bridge to later materials/circuit-mounting work; no tensor algebra prerequisite.
critical: The isotropic relations are not universal for wood, crystals, or composites.
ν=1/2 is an incompressible limiting model, not a finite-K substitution.

coverage.teaching: Estimate stiffness from differences in load and measured extension to cancel a constant zero offset. Distinguish specimen strain from fixture or grip compliance. Infer E only with known gauge length and original area. Propagate bounded F,L,A,E by monotone endpoint combinations, and diameter bounds through d². Compare displacement signal with instrument resolution without inventing probability distributions.
critical: A fit of apparatus extension can underestimate specimen E if fixture compliance is ignored.
Synthetic data are not physical measurements.
Allowed intervals and approximate relative sensitivities are different claims.

coverage.teaching: Use supplied stress and strain limits for hypothetical materials; limit equality is included and labeled limiting. A failed range check means the linear model cannot establish deformation, not necessarily that fracture occurs. In a loading-unloading investigation, once loading exceeds the declared range, later unloading values remain unestablished even when the load becomes small. Next lesson supplies additional plasticity and failure evidence.
critical: Do not extrapolate Hooke's law beyond its stated range.
Do not assume zero residual extension after an unsupported excursion.
No home tensioning, breaking, pressurizing, or suspended-load experiment is assigned.

Linear-domain checks, identification limits, isotropic assumptions, offset and fixture corrections, bounded measurements, instrument evidence, unloading history, and boundary-condition interpretation.

investigation.models: Separate axial, shear, and bulk modes. All are uniform hypothetical small-strain constitutive models about a stated reference, with stress and strain limits. Axial and shear use signed face force, original face area, and length or layer height. Bulk uses a nonnegative pressure increment and reference volume. No post-range material law, apparatus safety rating, buckling, bending, thermal change, viscoelasticity, or plastic unloading is modeled.
investigation.inputDesign: Discriminated model records: axial/shear mode,lengthM .01..5,areaMm2 .1..1000,modulusGPa .001..300,loadN -5000..5000,stressLimitMPa .01..1000,strainLimit .00001...05. Bulk mode,volumeCm3 .1..5000,modulusGPa .001..300,pressureMPa0..1000,pressureLimitMPa .01..1000,strainLimit .00001...05. Explicit units and finite-positive geometry/moduli; zero load admitted.
investigation.loading: Quasistatic load path0→signed requested peak→0, parameterized by loading stage0..2 rather than physical time. Exact bound sample inserted. At peakoutside supplied range, mark states strictly after first bound as unestablished, including unloading and finalzero load; no invented zero permanent set. At an admitted peak, reversible unloading retraces the constitutive curve and energy returns to zero.
investigation.equations: Axial sigmaMPa=F/Amm²,epsilon=sigmaMPa/(1000E_GPa),deltaM=epsilon*L,U=.5*F*deltaM. Shear tauMPa=F/Amm²,gamma=tauMPa/(1000G_GPa),shiftM=gamma*h,U=.5*F*shiftM. Bulk epsilonV=-pressureMPa/(1000K_GPa),deltaVcm3=epsilonV*Vcm3,U=pressureMPa²*Vcm3/(2000K_GPa). Stressbound=min(suppliedstresslimit,1000modulusGPa*strainlimit); compare absolute demand foraxial/shear. Constitutiveoutputsnullwhenunestablished; appliedstressandhistoryflagremainknown.
investigation.predictions: Peak signed stress (bulk pressure increase labeled separately), range decision, and peak strain/deformation only for admitted peaks. If outside, require an explicit not-established decision rather than accepting an extrapolated numerical displacement as actual behavior.
investigation.outputs: Constitutive response and energy only for admitted history, applied-load and stress records, exact limiting state, modulus-versus-stiffness distinction, complete equivalent table, force/displacement or pressure/volume chart, schematic deformation explicitly magnified with actual numbers, and keyboard stage controls. Show rejected portions as unknown, never as a continued line. Comparison presets changeonevariable orboundarycondition andrequestfreshpredictions.

investigation.safety: Simulation only. No wire tensioning, overhead weights, breaking specimens, pressurizing containers, or physical shear fixture is assigned. Official equipment requirements have not been established by the public PHS231 lecture description.

independentChecks: Integrate linear force versus displacement and stress versus strain by independent quadrature.
Solve series and parallel constraints as independent small linear systems and check each member's stress.
Integrate spatial axial force for the self-weight case instead of substituting the closed form.
Check bulk deformation sign and pressure work through signed volume integration.
Verify Poisson/isotropic results using three normal-stress equations rather than identical E,G,K formula substitution.
Enumerate measurement-bound corners and diameter endpoints; test zero offset and fixture compliance separately.

resources.title: Stress, Strain, and Elastic Modulus
resources.use: Coverage check and free companion for axial, shear, and bulk definitions. Use original numerical examples and explicit signed convention rather than copying source examples.

resources.title: Elasticity and Plasticity
resources.use: Distinguish proportional/elastic range and unsupported extrapolation; full plasticity and fracture reasoning belongs in m08-l03.

resources.title: Engineering Mechanics I: Isotropic Elasticity, Lecture 22
resources.use: PDF opened and checked for energy-based separation of volumetric and shear response and the assumptions behind isotropic constitutive equations. Optional extension; full tensor mathematics is not required.

resources.title: SI Guide: Rules for Units and Prefixes
resources.use: Verify that a prefix is inseparable from its unit and is raised to the power in area or volume conversions; printed unit conventions.
